title: Characteristics of storage devices
starter: You are buying storage for a school trip camera. Write the five questions you would ask before choosing.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: The six characteristics
facts: Capacity: how much it holds. Speed: how quickly data is read and written.
Portability: how easy it is to carry. Durability: how well it survives knocks.
Reliability: how likely it is to keep working. Cost: usually per gigabyte.
stations.challenge: Which two characteristics matter most for a school server, and why?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Capacity: how much it holds. Speed: how quickly data is read and written.
Also credit: Portability: how easy it is to carry. Durability: how well it survives knocks.

questions.q: Which of these are characteristics used to compare storage devices? Select all that apply.
What does durability mean for a storage device?
questions.a: How well it survives being knocked, dropped or moved

stations.name: Magnetic: the card
facts: Capacity: very high, several terabytes. Cost: lowest per gigabyte.
Speed: moderate. Portability: poor for internal drives, moderate for external.
Durability: poor, because of moving parts. Reliability: good while it stays still.
stations.challenge: Fill in the Top Trumps card for a hard disk drive.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Capacity: very high, several terabytes. Cost: lowest per gigabyte.
Also credit: Speed: moderate. Portability: poor for internal drives, moderate for external.

questions.q: What is a hard disk drive's biggest advantage?
questions.a: A very large capacity at a low cost per gigabyte
Moving parts make it fragile and slower than solid state

stations.name: Optical: the card
facts: Capacity: low, from 700 MB to 50 GB. Cost: very low per disc.
Speed: slow. Portability: excellent, thin and light.
Durability: poor, easily scratched. Reliability: good if stored carefully.
stations.challenge: Fill in the Top Trumps card for a Blu-ray disc.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Capacity: low, from 700 MB to 50 GB. Cost: very low per disc.
Also credit: Speed: slow. Portability: excellent, thin and light.

questions.q: Why are optical discs still used to distribute films and games?
questions.a: They are very cheap to produce in huge numbers and easy to post

questions.q: Which characteristic is an optical disc weakest on?

stations.name: Solid state: the card
facts: Capacity: high and rising. Cost: highest per gigabyte of the three.
Speed: fastest. Portability: excellent. Durability: excellent, no moving parts.
Reliability: very good, though cells do wear out after many writes.
stations.challenge: Fill in the Top Trumps card for an SSD.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Capacity: high and rising. Cost: highest per gigabyte of the three.
Also credit: Speed: fastest. Portability: excellent. Durability: excellent, no moving parts.

questions.q: Why is solid state storage chosen for laptops and phones?
questions.a: It is fast, light, silent and survives being carried around

questions.q: What eventually limits the life of flash memory?
questions.a: Each cell can only be written a limited number of times

stations.name: Head to head
facts: Fastest: solid state. Cheapest per gigabyte: magnetic.
Most portable: optical and small solid state devices.
Toughest: solid state. Biggest archive on a budget: tape.
stations.challenge: Which device wins on each characteristic?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Fastest: solid state. Cheapest per gigabyte: magnetic.
Also credit: Most portable: optical and small solid state devices.

questions.q: Which type of storage does each statement describe best?
questions.a: Cheapest per gigabyte for very large amounts = Magnetic; Fastest read and write speeds = Solid state; Cheapest way to send a film to millions of homes = Optical; Most durable when carried around = Solid state; Easily scratched = Optical; Contains moving parts that can fail = Magnetic

stations.name: Justify your choice
facts: Exam answers need the characteristic and the reason.
'An SSD, because it is fast and has no moving parts, so it survives being carried' scores; 'an SSD because it's better' doesn't.
Mention capacity, speed, portability, durability, reliability or cost by name.
stations.challenge: Write a full justification for the storage in a digital camera.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Exam answers need the characteristic and the reason.
Also credit: 'An SSD, because it is fast and has no moving parts, so it survives being carried' scores; 'an SSD because it's better' doesn't.

questions.q: Which is the best exam answer?
questions.a: An SSD, because it has no moving parts, so it is durable enough to be carried around all day

questions.q: A student writes 'a hard disk, because it is cheap'. How could it be improved?
questions.a: Say cheap per gigabyte, and link it to needing a lot of storage on a budget

final.name: Final challenge: Top Trumps

questions.q: Which device does each statement describe?
questions.a: Several terabytes, cheap, with spinning platters = Hard disk; About 25 GB, thin, light and easily scratched = Optical disc; The fastest of the four, with no moving parts = SSD; Read in sequence, ideal for huge cheap archives = Tape; Best for a laptop that gets carried everywhere = SSD; Best for distributing a film to millions of homes = Optical disc; Best value for a school server's bulk storage = Hard disk; Best for backing up 500 TB for ten years = Tape

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State two characteristics used to compare storage devices.
points: Most portable: optical and small solid state devices.
Fastest: solid state. Cheapest per gigabyte: magnetic.
Toughest: solid state. Biggest archive on a budget: tape.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: Explain why an SSD is more suitable than a hard disk for a laptop.
points: Capacity: how much it holds. Speed: how quickly data is read and written.
Portability: how easy it is to carry. Durability: how well it survives knocks.
Reliability: how likely it is to keep working. Cost: usually per gigabyte.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 4.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
